properties.description:
* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southwestern Grand County in east central Utah...

* WHEN...Until 1045 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos. Some
low-water crossings may become impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 841 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause arroyo and small stream flooding.
Between 0.2 and 0.6 inches of rain have fallen.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Tenmile Wash, Little Grand Wash and Tenmile Canyon.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
The Tenmile Wash, Little Grand Wash and Tenmile Canyon drainages.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.areaDesc: Buncombe, NC; Henderson, NC
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 12 at 10:20PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory is extended for the following rivers in North
Carolina...

French Broad River Near at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W Fletcher
affecting Buncombe and Henderson Counties.

.Excessive runoff from a widespread 4 to 5 inch storm total rainfall
will maintain flooding along the French Broad River.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive runoff continues.

* WHERE...French Broad River near at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W
Fletcher.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Action/Advisory Stage. The French Broad
River has exceeded bankfull at the gauge site. Isolated farmland
flooding is expected across the French Broad River Valley from
Etowah downstream to Avery Creek upstream of the gauge site. At
10.7 feet, Action Stage Flooding continues. Butler Bridge Road is
inundated with up to 6 inches of floodwaters from the French Broad
River, forcing road closure.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 PM EDT Monday the stage was 10.7 feet and falling.
- Forecast...The river is expected to start falling slowly
overnight, and fall to 9 ft feet Friday evening.
- Action/Advisory Stage is 10.0 feet.
- Minor Flood Stage is 13.0 feet.
properties.instruction:
If you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around and find an
alternative route. Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

For detailed information including observed and forecast stages,
flood impacts, flood history, FEMA Flood Hazard Layers, and more,
please visit: https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/GSP

The next statement should be issued Tuesday morning before 800 AM
EDT.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 12 at 6:14PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Thursday into the weekend, a series of low pressure systems will
move toward Southeast Alaska, bringing widespread moderate to heavy
rainfall and gale force winds to the Gulf. Strong winds are also
expected for coastal and southern panhandle communities. While the
exact timing and impacts of the system are still being refined,
confidence is continuing to increase that this will be a more
impactful system for Southeast Alaska.

Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to monitor the
developing situation and update our forecast.

NWSheadline: HEAVY RAIN AND GUSTY WINDS THURSDAY INTO WEEKEND

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 12 at 1:50PM SST by NWS Pago Pago  AS
properties.description:
ESFPPG

An active trough to the north is projected to drift southward and
move over the territory by Thursday night. Widespread showers may
be heavy and persistent at times with the possibility of thunderstorms.
Landslides will also be possible along steep mountainous terrain.
Impacts could begin as early as Thursday and are expected to
persist through the weekend. While there is still uncertainty in
the exact magnitude and duration of rainfall, plan now for wet
conditions that could persist through at least Sunday.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through our
internet page (www.weather.gov/ppg), local media, social media,
and our NOAA Radio broadcasts.
